requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: UFW was enabled with a default inbound REJECT policy and remained active and enabled after a demonstrated reboot. Pre/post checksums of its persistent configuration matched, and the lifecycle boot IDs independently confirm the reboot.
TCP port 22 was explicitly allowed and successful inbound SSH handshakes were observed from an isolated namespace both before and after reboot.
TCP port 8080 was explicitly allowed, and an isolated inbound client received HTTP 200 from a confirmed listener both before and after reboot.
The firewall used a default inbound REJECT policy. Connections to a confirmed TCP 9090 listener were refused before and after reboot, with the UFW reject counter increasing.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The firewall's intended allow/reject behavior was directly exercised before and after a confirmed node restart, and persistent configuration remained unchanged. The mandatory restart evidence is complete and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations.
limitations: Behavioral traffic tests used IPv4. IPv6 allowance and rejection are supported by the displayed UFW IPv6 configuration but were not exercised with an IPv6 client.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Firewall changes directly implemented the task; the namespace, veth links, test listeners, logs, and PID files were bounded verification fixtures and were removed. SSH host-key initialization and service recovery supported the required SSH behavior and corrected the failure exposed by testing. The reboot established persistence and fulfilled the provider restart protocol. Final observations show no failed services, no test listeners or files, and healthy package state.
